habit.lifeForm.basis: RHS plant record: a large, vigorous deciduous climber. Bean, of C. viticella: 'a deciduous, partly woody climber' whose summer growth 'dies back in winter nearly to the older stem'.

habit.heightM.basis: RHS plant record: ultimate height 2.5-4 m. Clematis on the Web gives the same; the International Clematis Society 10 to 15 ft 'depending on local conditions'.

habit.spreadM.basis: RHS plant record: ultimate spread 1-1.5 m.

habit.flowersWhere.value: mostly on the upper half of the new wood
habit.flowersWhere.basis: International Clematis Society, Clematis of the Month, October 1997: it flowers by midsummer, mostly on the upper half of the new wood, and the flowers hide most of the foliage.

stem.surface.value: slender, ribbed, slightly downy when young
stem.surface.basis: Bean, of C. viticella: 'stems slender, ribbed, and slightly downy when young'. No description of the cultivar's stems was found; it is taken to be like the species.

stem.colour.basis: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria, Horticultural Flora, of C. viticella: a semi-woody climber with reddish stems. Of the species, not of the cultivar.

stem.twining.basis: Darwin, The Movements and Habits of Climbing Plants (1875), of C. viticella var. venosa: 'the power of spirally twining is completely lost'; the young internodes still sweep small ellipses.

leaf.arrangement.basis: Bean, of the genus: 'The leaves are always in pairs at each joint'.

leaf.division.basis: RHS plant record: 'mid-green leaves divided into 5 leaflets'. Bean, of C. viticella: pinnate, the primary divisions trifoliolate.

leaf.leafletCount.basis: RHS plant record, of this cultivar: leaves 'divided into 5 leaflets'. The usual leaf; see leaf.leafletPairsMost for the fullest.

leaf.leafletPairsMost.basis: Darwin (1875), of C. viticella var. venosa: 'three pairs of lateral leaflets and a terminal one, all supported on rather long sub-petioles'. Of a variety of the species, not of this cultivar: the largest leaf drawn.

leaf.basalDivisionLeaflets.basis: Bean, of C. viticella: pinnate, 'the primary divisions trifoliolate'. Darwin: the stalk of each of the lowest pair of leaflets usually divides into three. Of the species; drawn on some leaves of the cultivar, on the lowest pair only.

leaf.lengthM.basis: Bean, of C. viticella: leaves '4 or 5 in. long', in metres. Flora Europaea gives 10-13 cm. No figure was found for the cultivar; the growth model's organs.leafLengthM takes it as the same.

leaf.leafletLengthM.basis: Bean, of C. viticella: leaflets '3/4 to 2 1/2 in. long', in metres. Of the species.

leaf.leafletShape.basis: Bean, of C. viticella: leaflets lance-shaped to broadly ovate. Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria: 'ovate to lanceolate'.

leaf.leafletMargin.basis: Bean, of C. viticella: leaflets untoothed but often two- or three-lobed.

leaf.leafletWidthToLength.basis: No width is given anywhere read. Chosen to span Bean's 'lance-shaped' to 'broadly ovate': a leaflet four tenths to seven tenths as wide as it is long.

leaf.leafletStalk.basis: Darwin (1875), of C. viticella var. venosa: the leaflets are 'all supported on rather long sub-petioles'. No length is given.

leaf.axisPosture.value: bent downwards at each pair of leaflets, the end leaflet bent down most; the side leaflets angled a little upwards
leaf.axisPosture.basis: Darwin (1875), of C. viticella var. venosa: the main petiole bends angularly downwards where each pair of leaflets arises and the stalk of the end leaflet is bent down at a right angle, so that the whole leaf is a hook; a leaf that catches nothing 'ultimately grows straight'.

leaf.stalkShare.basis: The length of the leaf stalk below the first pair of leaflets, as a share of the whole leaf. No measurement was found; chosen from the look of a pinnate clematis leaf.

leaf.colour.basis: RHS plant record: 'mid-green leaves'. International Clematis Society: the foliage is a fresh green that darkens through the season.

inflorescence.type.value: flowers solitary or up to three together on a branched stalk from a leaf axil
inflorescence.type.basis: Bean, of C. viticella: flowers solitary on stalks 2 to 4 in. long, 'or several on a branched stalk'. The key of the Manual of the Alien Plants of Belgium, after Flora Europaea: flowers solitary or up to three. Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria: 'terminal or axillary'.

inflorescence.flowerCount.basis: What the model draws at each flowering node: one cyme of three, the end flower and two side flowers. The published range is one to three in an axil, and a node has two axils; the engine allows one flower record to a node. Three is chosen to stand for what a node of a well-grown plant carries; it is not a count.

inflorescence.stalkLengthM.basis: Bean, of C. viticella: flowers on stalks '2 to 4 in. long', in metres. Of the species, whose flowers are less than half as wide as the cultivar's.

inflorescence.lengthM.basis: The length of a cyme from the leaf axil to the face of its end flower. This is what the growth model's organs.racemeLengthM measures, what RenderFlower.lengthM carries, and what the flower model's authoredSize stands for. No such length is published; it is set so that a flower, drawn half as wide as the cyme is long, is 6.5 to 9.5 cm across (flower.widthM).

inflorescence.held.basis: HelpMeFind record of the cultivar: bloom form single, semi-nodding. Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria, of C. viticella: flowers nodding. Bean, of the cultivar: 'opening flat'.

flower.widthM.basis: Clematis on the Web: flower diameter 5-10 cm. RHS: 'to 10cm across'. Bean: 'about 4 in. wide'. HelpMeFind: about 3.5 in on average.

flower.tepalCount.basis: RHS plant record: 'four to six broad, velvety textured deep purple sepals'. Clematis on the Web: tepals 4-6.

flower.tepalShape.value: broad, long-pointed, the tip and margin recurved
flower.tepalShape.basis: Clematis on the Web: tepals 'long-pointed, tip and margin recurved'. RHS: 'broad'. International Clematis Society: newly open 'a conspicuously neat circlet', the margins later 'irregularly tucked back'.

flower.tepalWidthToLength.basis: No tepal measurements were found. 'Broad' (RHS) is drawn as a tepal six to seven tenths as wide as long, the broadest where a flower has four.

flower.colour.basis: RHS plant record: 'deep purple'. Clematis on the Web: 'deep purple flowers'. Bean: 'deep purple'. International Clematis Society: 'brownish purple with a yellow eye' when newly open; red streaks or highlights on late flowers.

flower.stamenColour.basis: RHS plant record: 'a small boss of cream stamens'. Bean: cream-coloured stamens. Clematis on the Web: stamens creamy-yellow. Filaments and anthers are not described apart.

flower.bossWidthToFlower.basis: RHS: 'a small boss' of stamens. No measurement was found; drawn a quarter as wide as the flower.

flower.budShape.basis: Not described for this cultivar. The International Clematis Society describes the buds of 'Pagoda', another clematis of the Viticella Group, as 'ovoid to conical' and 'typically viticella in shape' (https://internationalclematissociety.org/?p=1019); taken as the same here.

fruit.type.value: a head of achenes with very small tails that are not feathery
fruit.type.basis: Bean, of C. viticella: 'seed-vessels broad and short' with 'very small tails devoid of the feathery covering'. The Manual of the Alien Plants of Belgium tells the species by its glabrous styles. Of the species; nothing was found on the seed heads of the cultivar.

fruit.headWidthM.basis: No measurement was found. A head of 'broad and short' achenes (Bean) is drawn 18 to 26 mm across, tails included.

hold.organ.value: the leaf stalk and the stalks of the leaflets
hold.organ.basis: Darwin (1875), of C. viticella var. venosa: the main petiole, the sub-petioles and the branches of the lowest sub-petioles are all sensitive and clasp a stick; the under side of the bent end portion is the most sensitive. Bean, of the genus: they 'support themselves by means of the leaf-stalks, which curl round any slender support'.

hold.afterClasping.basis: Darwin (1875): a clasped petiole of C. calycina swells in two or three days to nearly twice the thickness of its fellow and becomes tough and rigid; the same happens in the other species 'in a less strongly marked manner'. Of C. vitalba: clasped petioles become stiff, hard and polished and outlast the leaf.

hold.heldDiameterMm.basis: The thickness of the support a clasp is drawn round: the 5 mm cable of the specimen frame and the example Bowers, which is the only thing in them this plant can hold by itself (the growth model takes 8 mm as the stoutest it can grasp). A choice about the drawing, not a fact about the plant.

hold.stalkThicknessMm.basis: Thickness of a leaf stalk where it has clasped. No measurement was found: a wiry stalk about a millimetre thick.

hold.claspReachM.basis: The reach of a clasp, from the stem round the far side of what it holds: the 5 mm cable, the stalk's own millimetre on each side, and a little play. This, not the length of the stalk, is what the growth model gives as appendages.leafStalkLengthM and what RenderAppendage.lengthM carries, because the engine puts a clasping stalk where the stem lies against the cable: the rest of the stalk is the stalk of the leaf drawn at the same node. Worked out from the cable, not measured on a plant.
